title: docs(adr-0131): amend D13's reach — the legacy-anchor retirement leaves it for the walled posture, on the 17.x line
body:
Fixes #18413

Governed surface (`docs/adr/**`), one file, one amendment: `docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md` (+129 / -4). Draft, `skip-changeset`, **maintainer-merged** — no seat flips this ready, queues it, or arms auto-merge (Prime Directive #14). `node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --test docs/adr/0131-…md` answers **GOVERNED**, 1 of 1 path.

## 1. The ruling and its authority

Maintainer ruling, option **B** on #18336, taken in session `session_01LmoCFLwGkcAGefVf7jryEV` on 2026-09-16T09:54Z and recorded on that card (`#issuecomment-5695555178`). The option text the maintainer selected, verbatim and untranslated:

> **B — #11663 设计说了算**
> 修订 ADR-0131 D13，把这两个符号从其退役清单里摘掉，本卡留在 17.x 线执行。

Three things it decided: #11663's design governs this leg for these two symbols; the work stays on the **17.x** line (not re-targeted to v18, not gated by #15193); the two symbols leave D13's retirements. Recorded under Prime Directive #13 — reversing a recorded decision needs an amended record, and this PR is that act. ADR-0131 stays **Accepted**; only the staging of one leg moves.

## 2. Reading correction — where the symbols actually were

The card states that D13's list names both symbols. Measured on `origin/main` `32be735e5`, that is not where they are:

| symbol | `docs/adr/` | `docs/` | `packages/` (positive control) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reportLegacyPlatformAdminGrant` | **1** — ADR-0131 `:362`, inside **D5** | 3 | 15 |
| `resetLegacyPlatformAdminGrantReport` | **0** | 0 | 17 |

D13's own retirement list (`:641–659` on `main`) names neither. What the record actually carries is D5's sentence 「`reportLegacyPlatformAdminGrant` and the legacy unscoped anchor retire with D13」 — an **assignment** to D13, which is what the ruling reaches. So this amendment edits **D5, D14 and §7** and leaves D13's list as it stands. The substance of the card is unaffected: before, the retirement was D13's and therefore v18's; after, it is #11663's and 17.x's. `premise_still_valid: true`, with this correction.

## 3. The D13 text, before and after

**D5, before:**

> `PLATFORM_ADMIN` derives from `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL` (#13514 L4) — configuration, not a row. The `single`-posture first-user promotion (Choice 4A), which today writes an `admin_full_access` grant row with a NULL organization, writes it **owned by the Default Organization** instead; under a walled posture no grant row is written (unchanged). **`reportLegacyPlatformAdminGrant` and the legacy unscoped anchor retire with D13. No NULL grant row is ever produced.**

**D5, after** (the bolded half is what moved):

> … under a walled posture no grant row is written (unchanged). **That ownership change is C3's, on the v18 line, and it is unchanged by the 2026-09-16 ruling — so no NULL grant row is ever produced once C3 has landed; until then the `single` row carries the NULL organization it carries today, and D10's migration is what clears it. The legacy unscoped anchor retires with D13 for the `single` posture only: its walled half, together with the two symbols that carry the migration window — `reportLegacyPlatformAdminGrant` and `resetLegacyPlatformAdminGrantReport` — left D13 on 2026-09-16 and retire on the 17.x line under #11663's design instead (#18336; see the Amendment at the end). The `single` anchor's own disposition is #11979's (Choice 4B), which this record does not pre-empt.**

Plus: a `**Amended** (2026-09-17, …)` clause on the status line; one **named exception** written into D14; the §7 post-17.2 audit line given the same exception; and a full `## Amendment (2026-09-17, #18413)` record at the end of the file carrying the authority, the two standing constraints, the closed question and the D14 reconciliation.

## 4. How each standing constraint is honoured

Both are quoted verbatim and untranslated in the amendment. Neither was touched by the ruling, and both still bind.

**Choice 4A** — maintainer, 2026-09-08, #16682 comment `5587754690`:

> The rest of Choice 4A (#11974, 2026-08-25) stands: **retiring the walled write must not retire the `single` one**

Honoured: the amendment narrows the retirement to the **walled posture** in every place it names it — D5, D14's exception and the §7 line each say "walled". The `single` write, its grant row and its zero-config first-user promotion are stated as surviving until #11979 (Choice 4B) disposes of them. Nothing in the diff removes or narrows the `single` half.

**The zero-config constraint** — maintainer, 2026-09-16, the same session as the ruling:

> 比如临时启动的开发环境，我不可能去配置啊

Honoured: the amendment states that `single` keeps its zero-config first-user promotion, and it does not touch the derivation that delivers it — the unscoped-grant read at §6/§6b of `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`. The amendment also records the mechanical reason the all-postures reading was never available for this leg: the deprecation pointer is **already posture-keyed** (`postureEnforcesWall(resolveTenancyPosture())` at the §6b-config arm), so under `single` there is no pointer behaviour to retire at all.

## 5. The open question — CLOSED in the text, not deferred

The STOP condition did not trigger. The two standing constraints do **not** conflict with the D13 change: the change *reduces* what retires, and a reduction cannot retire the `single` write; the zero-config channel is the unscoped read, which is not the reporter and is untouched. Closing the question needs no new maintainer decision — only two ruled texts that the option-B ruling explicitly left alone. The decision sentence, as it is written into the ADR:

> **Decision (2026-09-17, #18413).** The `single`-posture first-user grant row **still becomes owned by the Default Organization**. That is D5's own answer, accepted by the maintainer on 2026-09-04 (§6, one of the four open questions answered 「接受你的建议」), and the option-B ruling does not touch it. It still lands **on the v18 line, under C3** (§8), exactly where it was before this amendment. **Until C3 lands, the row keeps the NULL organization it carries today** — the state D10's migration exists to clear — and D1's NOT NULL constraint still reaches that table only when D10 reports zero for it.

**Why the drop moves no row** — measured, not argued. `reportLegacyPlatformAdminGrant` (`packages/core/src/security/platform-admin.ts:351`) is a once-per-process `warn` naming one holder and pointing at `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`; `resetLegacyPlatformAdminGrantReport` (`:371`) drops that latch for tests. Neither writes the grant row, neither reads its `organization`, and neither participates in the derivation that confers `PLATFORM_ADMIN` — that is the `unscopedUserPsIds` read at `resolve-authz-context.ts:839` and the check at `:928`, untouched by this amendment. So the 17.x retirement this amendment authorizes adds no NULL row, removes none, and re-owns none. **D1 and D10 are therefore unaffected**: the NULL-ownership question is not created by the drop and is not answered by it — it is answered by D5, on D5's own schedule.

## 6. Reconciliation with D14 and with #15193

**D14** 「⛔ No 17.x card narrows or removes an arm, adds a name column beside an id column, or ships a half of this record」 gains exactly one named exception, written into D14 itself. Two independent reasons, either sufficient:

1. **It is not a half of this record.** The ruling assigned the leg to #11663's design. Work this record no longer governs cannot be a half of it.
2. **It narrows no arm.** The arms D14 fences are the drivers' `orWhereNull` arms inside `applyTenantScope` — the record's own vocabulary (D13 `:641`, D14 `:674`, §7 `:836` "the arms are inside `applyTenantScope` … there are **two**"; the reads in `resolve-authz-context.ts` are called "NULL readings", never arms). The walled legacy-anchor read and its pointer are neither of those, add no column, and move no row.

The exception is written as **exhausted** by that leg and those two symbols: every other retirement in D13 keeps D14's fence and stays gated on D10's zero-NULL report.

**#15193** (the v18 gate, open p1) — confirmed it no longer gates #18336 under this ruling, and the amendment says so in D14's exception and in its "What the ruling decided" list. #15193's own rule binds "every ADR-0131 execution card"; the option-B ruling took this leg out of that set, and the ruling comment states it directly (「本卡留在 17.x 线，⛔ 不改挂 `target:v18`、⛔ 不阻塞于 #15193」). ⛔ No label or body of #15193 is touched by this PR — that is #18336's own re-pointing, out of scope here.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

**改了什么**:只改了一个文件 —— ADR-0131。把「那两个平台管理员报告符号在 v18 退役」这条安排**摘掉**,改成:它们按 #11663 的设计、在 **17.x** 线上退役,而且**只限 walled(隔离墙)姿态**。同时在文本里把一个悬着的问题**答死**:`single` 姿态那条授权行的组织归属不变 —— 仍然按 ADR-0131 原本的答案改成「默认组织所有」,仍然在 v18 的 C3 那张卡上做;在那之前它保持今天的 NULL,由 D10 的迁移来清。另外给 D14 加了一条**具名例外**,并更正了 §7 的一句话。⛔ 没动任何代码、没动任何其它 ADR。

**为什么改**:2026-09-16 您在 #18336 上选了 **B —— #11663 设计说了算**,并要求修订 ADR-0131 D13。ADR-0131 今天是 Accepted 且在 `main` 上,如果不先改它,#18336 的移除一落地,代码就和一份已接受的 ADR 直接抵触。次序是固定的:**先本卡 → 再 #18336**。另外您在同一会话说的「比如临时启动的开发环境,我不可能去配置啊」,加上 2026-09-08 关于 Choice 4A 的裁决(「retiring the walled write must not retire the `single` one」),这两条本次裁决**一个字都没碰**,所以范围被机械地收成「只限 walled」——零配置开发环境不受任何影响。

**风险与代价(含回滚)**:代价很小。改的是治理记录的措辞与分线,**不改变任何运行时行为**:被摘掉的两个符号一个是「每进程一次的提醒日志」、一个是「测试用的开关复位」,它们既不写那条授权行、也不读它的组织字段,所以这次修订**不新增、不删除、不改写任何一行数据的归属**,D1(非空约束)和 D10(零-NULL 迁移)完全不受影响。风险面只有一个:D14 原本禁止「17.x 上只发本记录的一半」,现在它多了一条例外 —— 例外写成**一次性用尽**(只覆盖这条腿和这两个符号),D13 其余退役仍然照旧受 D10 把关。回滚成本为零:单文件 revert 即可,没有代码、没有迁移、没有发布物。

**席位意见**:(留空,待维护者裁定)
